summary: This plan sets up a simple mobile money wallet service for your shop's customers in Accra. A customer opens a wallet with their name and phone number, and each phone number can have only one wallet. Money can be put into a wallet and sent from one wallet to another. You can check any wallet's balance and see its full history of deposits and transfers, with the balance right after each one. All amounts are in Ghana cedis, are always more than zero and have at most two decimal places (pesewas). To keep every total exact to the pesewa, amounts are stored as whole pesewas, so there are no rounding mistakes. You had no preference about who uses the service, so I chose the simplest option: there are no logins or PINs, and anyone using the service can make deposits and transfers. There are no fees, and taking money out as cash is not included, as you asked. Some questions for you; none of these are in the plan unless you ask for them. (1) Without a PIN or staff-only access, anyone who knows a wallet's details could send its money or view its history. Do you want some protection for this? (2) You did not say whether there should be limits on how much can be deposited or sent at once or per day. Do you want any? (3) Should a wallet's history and balance be private to its owner or your staff? (4) Should phone numbers be checked for a valid Ghana format?

data.name: Wallet
fields: wallet number (given automatically when the wallet is opened)
phone number (only one wallet per phone number)
current balance (kept in whole pesewas, starts at zero)
date and time the wallet was opened

data.name: History entry
fields: type: deposit, money sent, or money received
the other wallet involved (for money sent or received)
the wallet's balance right after this entry

endpoints.does: Opens a new wallet with the customer's name and phone number. The balance starts at zero.
Shows a wallet's owner name, phone number and current balance.
Puts an amount of money into the wallet and adds a deposit entry to its history, showing the new balance.
Sends an amount from this wallet to another wallet, chosen by the receiver's phone number. Both wallets get a history entry showing their own balance afterwards.
Lists every deposit and transfer for the wallet in order. Each one shows the type, the amount, the other wallet involved and the balance right after it.

rules: Refuse to open a wallet if the name or phone number is missing.
Refuse to open a wallet for a phone number that already has a wallet.
Refuse any deposit or transfer amount that is zero or less.
Refuse any amount with more than two decimal places (smaller than one pesewa).
Refuse a transfer that is larger than the sending wallet's current balance, so no balance ever goes below zero.
Refuse a transfer where the sending and receiving wallets are the same.
Refuse a deposit, transfer, balance check or history request for a wallet that does not exist, including a transfer to a phone number with no wallet.
A transfer either completes fully or does not happen at all. Money is never taken from one wallet without being added to the other.
All money is counted in whole pesewas, so every balance and total is exact with no rounding.
